I only have 1.5 mu, and I grow cotton on all of it, so I will keep the whole plot in cotton this year instead of splitting land into other crops. With a small area and some family members working off-farm, I will manage for steady output and lower labor risk rather than chasing the highest possible yield. I have 10 years of experience, so I will use an improved cotton seed rather than traditional seed because I want more stable emergence and boll setting. Since I have well irrigation, I will rely on several irrigations to avoid drought stress at key stages. For fertilization, I will put in moderate nitrogen and balanced phosphorus and potassium because cotton needs steady nutrition, but on such a small plot I do not want excessive vegetative growth. I will plough before planting because I want a clean, deep seedbed at the start of the season. I will also plan several pesticide applications because cotton usually faces insect and disease pressure through the season, and I would rather protect yield early than lose bolls later. My goal is stable management, manageable labor, and a solid yield from the whole 1.5 mu.
